name: Living jobs end to end at the desk
summary:
On living jobs the desk does most of what Anthony asked, and the agents now carry the evening. On a 120-shot Home Transition, two presses (Name 120 shots, OK) gave every line a name, a category, a count, a condition and a value in one pass with no further prompt. A confirmed Job Plan vendor filled every Donate, Sell and Junk line, marked "from the Job Plan". The verbal-approval rule holds where it is enforced: only the firearm and the line going to a Havellin person reached the request, and the letter reads well. Signing a charity or vendor pickup on the iPad works.

From the concierge's seat, the cost is in what is left over. Agent Two values every living line, so 24 of 28 "Unsure" flags sat on Keep, Move and Junk lines that no living paper prints. A name typed at the desk does not count as reviewed, and a rename after the tick unticks the line. Photographs with "nothing to list" stay as lines that block the client's sign-off. A Home Transition that sells has no proceeds-statement tool, so each lot's gross and fees are typed by hand in the line's record. A living client's own shotgun kept or moved stays "held" for good. The selection also survives every bulk action and filter, so Remove lines took 20 reviewed Move lines hidden behind a filter.

From the family's and their CPA's seat, the Contents Record, the one paper the client signs, can carry an IN PROGRESS stamp and the sign-off together. It lists Hold lines as "not recorded" without withholding the signature. It prints the desk's words "Distribute" and "Move", and it goes quiet about a flagged piece once Agent Two's unreviewed figure lands. The donation papers fall short of what a deduction needs: no date (even after the app witnessed it), no valuation method, no $5,000 appraisal warning, and no "no goods or services" sentence on the charity's acknowledgement. Estate apparatus still leaks into living screens and the CSV (Specific Bequest, §732.402, "usually the date of death"), and the playbook still says nothing is valued on living work.

None of this needs a new rule: most fixes ask an existing rule one more question. The two exceptions are a new-home room on Move lines and iPad signing of the Contents Record, both natural extensions of the desk.
works_well: Two presses name, room-check, value and grade a whole living house. b1.js: 'Name 120 shots' plus OK gave 'lines 130 named 120 valued 120' in 5.2 s with stubbed agents, with no further prompt.

A confirmed Job Plan vendor fills the recipient where a person sets the disposition. b1.js: Donate filled Goodwill, Sell filled Kodner and Junk filled Haul-It, each marked 'from the Job Plan' (invFillPlanChannel).

The written-release rule on a client's own home holds. b1.js: only the shotgun and the line to Ashley Jerome counted ('2 items need written approval'). Donate, Sell and Junk went on the client's word, and the Releases bar stayed hidden until something needed it.

The living release request reads as a letter. b10.js: it explains why a line going to someone who works with Havellin is on it, in plain words, and asks one initial for the firearm batch, stating the dealer route.

iPad sign-out for a charity and a vendor works end to end. b4.js: the pad was drawn on, Sign and file made the PDF (htmlToPdf, uploadFile), and the Donations card and the row read the charity receipt as on file.
The Contents Record puts its gaps above the list. It reads 'kept by the client' on Keep and prints the new-home address on Move, and withholds the sign-off while a line is undecided (b1, b8).

The firearm path on living explains itself. b4.js: the dealer-route prompt names the person and the dealer, the record then reads 'To Susan Hale, through Jupiter Gun Shop FFL … recorded by Ashley Jerome', and only the authority remains.
Home Cleanout's proceeds statement: typing the vendor ticked all six of its lots in the dialog (b5.js).
Home Editing withholds Move where there is no new home. b5.js options: '—|Auction|Consign|Distribute|Donate|Hold|Junk|Keep|Sell'.
No page errors in any run, and no horizontal overflow at 1440, 1024 or 390 px (b7.js).
measurements: Whole pipeline on a fresh living house: 120 shots named, room-checked and valued in 5,158 ms (b1.js, stubbed agents). 400 shots in 8,626 ms including setup (b6.js).

Presses to finish a 400-shot living house where the field chips decided 367 of 433 lines: 2 to name (button + OK), then 3 per decided group (Select all, Mark reviewed, Clear), so 14 presses for 368 lines (b6.js). Each line left undecided then costs 3-4 presses plus typing: 2 taps on the select, the recipient where it leaves, 1 Reviewed tick. That is 96-128 presses for the 32 left. The 33 nothing-to-list lines cost 4 presses together (chip, Select all, Remove lines, OK).

One typical line, photo to decided and reviewed: 1 press (Reviewed) when the field chip and the Job Plan vendor did the rest. 3-4 presses when undecided. A corrected name adds the typing and a second Reviewed tick after Agent Two's re-value lands (b11.js: rev true, then false, after the rename).

Render cost at 433 lines on the laptop (b6.js): renderInventoryTab 180 ms. One disposition change took 493 ms to the next frame, because the whole tab re-renders. The desk is 16,277 DOM nodes and 44,078 px tall, and the Contents Record's html is 364,034 bytes.
Unsure on a living job with low-confidence ordinary lots (b7.js): 28 lines, of which Move 16, Keep 4, Junk 4 and Donate 4, so 24 of the 28 on lines no living paper prints a value for.
Touch targets at 1024 px, iPad landscape (b7.js): Reviewed box 14x14 px, disposition select 110x22 px, row 114 px tall. At 390 px: select 329x44 px, Reviewed box 13x44 px.
Agent Two on living: 120 of 120 photographed lines valued by itself (b1.js). A desk rename sent 1 research request, mode 'comps', nameChecked true, on a Keep line (b3.js).
verifier_note: The LIV report holds up well. I re-drove the important claims with my own scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/LIV-verify/ (v1.js to v4.js, outputs in v1.out to v4.out). They use the shared harness, the real Name / Value / Select all / Mark reviewed / chip / Remove lines / row selects, and a house where each field chip was given its Job Plan vendor the way _captureShot does it. The auditor's own b2 fixture skipped that step, which inflated its "no recipient" count; my v3 needed one Consign line to show it. Every defect, inconsistency and accuracy claim reproduced, with four exceptions. LIV-05 is overstated: the line's record has Authorized By and Approval Date boxes, and typing them clears the hold. LIV-10 is partly wrong: condition is printed, the record does say the figures are Havellin's estimates and not appraisals, and the filing date of the charity's receipt is printed. LIV-13 is overstated: the Close-out stage and Job Admin already carry 'Contents Record signed by the client: not yet', and only the close question is silent. LIV-23 is the other half of the same line of code (32987) as a Known item. Three proposals argue against recorded Domain rules without saying so (LIV-03, -06 and -07: 'Review gates nothing' and 'Every figure is unreviewed until looked at'). LIV-18 widens Agent One's write list, as its auditor noted. Two figures depend on the stub: LIV-06's unsure-by-disposition counts and the b6 timings were not re-measured. No page errors appeared in any of my runs.

findings.title: The ⚑ 'flagged for appraisal, no value recorded' warning disappears from the client's papers once Agent Two writes an unreviewed figure
findings.where: Contents Record (work bar), the release request and the Disposition Ledger badge; INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS 'flaggedUnvalued' test, havellin.html:32186-32187 (`!_invHasValue(r)`); agentValueAuto 38873 values every photographed living line by itself
findings.evidence: b9.js on Hale (9602), line l03 (oil painting, ⚑, Sell to Kodner). Before: 'l03 before {cautions:[flaggedUnvalued]}', 'CR before has the badge true'. After pressing 'Value 5 lines': 'l03 after {fmv:1200, valuedBy:agent, conf:high, cautions:[]}', 'CR after has the badge false'. The row still reads '⚑ appraise'. Since 2026-10-25b the naming run values every photographed line by itself, so in practice the badge never reaches the client.
findings.tc_impact: The concierge sees ⚑ appraise on the row while the client's paper says nothing. The family, or their CPA, signs a Contents Record with no sign that a piece the crew thought needed a specialist was sold on Havellin's unreviewed estimate. That is exactly the case Q82 put on the paper.
findings.proposal: Make the caution's test 'no figure from a person or an appraiser': `(!_invHasValue(r) || r.valuedBy === 'agent') && …`. Where an agent figure exists, the badge reads 'FLAGGED FOR APPRAISAL — ONLY HAVELLIN'S ESTIMATE ($1,200) ON RECORD' and its body adjusts to match. Initialling the line, or Waive, still clears it. This keeps Anthony's Q82 decision working under 2026-10-25b's automation.
findings.vnote: Ran on Hale (9602), line l03: an oil painting with ⚑, set to Sell to Kodner, no value. Before: cautions [flaggedUnvalued] and the Contents Record carries the badge. I pressed the real 'Value 5 lines' button; l03 went out in research mode and came back {fmv:1200, valuedBy:agent, valRev:false}. After: cautions [] and no badge on the Contents Record, while the desk row still reads '⚑ appraise'. The code agrees: INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS flaggedUnvalued tests `!_invHasValue(r)` (havellin.html:32187), and its own comment still says 'On living work nothing is valued', which agentValueAuto (38873) has made false. So the Q82 badge Anthony asked for disappears as soon as Agent Two's unreviewed figure lands, on the request, the Contents Record and the ledger alike.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v1.js → v1.out: 'l03 before {...cautions:[flaggedUnvalued]}', 'CR before: badge? true', 'l03 after {fmv:1200, valuedBy:agent ... cautions:[]}', 'CR after: badge? false', 'desk row l03 … ⚑ appraise'; havellin.html:32186-32187

findings.title: The selection survives bulk actions and filter changes, so Remove lines removes lines that are hidden off screen
findings.where: Bulk bar at the foot of the desk; _invPickGroup havellin.html:37284, _invBulkApply 37298 (never clears _invPick), setInvFlag / setInvRoom 37454-37458 (keep picks), invBulkRemove 29938 (acts on _invPicked, which includes hidden picks)
findings.evidence: b2.js, living Home Transition. Steps: Select all on Move (20 lines), Mark reviewed (the bar still read 20 selected), the 'Unnamed shots' chip, Select all (5 nothing-to-list lines), Remove lines. The confirm read 'Remove 25 lines … #1 Tufted linen three-seat sofa, #6 Mahogany drop-leaf side table … and 17 more', and afterwards the bar read 'Removed items & snapshots 25 removed'. b3.js: after Mark reviewed the bar read '6 selected'; with a room filter on, 'visible rows 9 | bar: 6 selected | of which ticked on screen 0'.
findings.tc_impact: Twenty reviewed Move lines vanished from the Contents Record and the move pile because a concierge working fast confirmed what looked like a five-line cleanup. They come back only if someone notices '25 removed'. Bulk 'Set disposition' would re-route the same hidden lines.
findings.proposal: Clear the selection after every bulk action, as Remove lines already does after itself, and on every filter change. Where picks are still hidden, invBulkRemove and _invBulkApply ask apart: '20 of the 25 selected are not on screen (Move · Living Room …). OK changes only the 5 on screen.'
findings.vnote: Reproduced through the real controls on a 36-shot living house. Select all on Move gave 12 selected. Mark reviewed left the bar at '12 selected'. Pressing the Unnamed shots chip showed 3 visible rows with the bar still at 12. Select all on screen made it 15. Remove lines showed a confirm naming '#1 Tufted linen three-seat sofa … and 7 more', and all 12 Move lines were gone (live Move lines 12 → 0). The bar never says how many selected lines are off screen. Its 'no longer match the filters' note appears only after a bulk apply, never after a chip press. The lines can be restored from Removed items, which is why this is high and not fix-now.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v2.js → v2.out: 'bar after Mark reviewed 12 selected', 'after the Unnamed chip: visible rows 3 | bar 12 selected', 'bar now 15 selected', REMOVE CONFIRM text, 'Move lines live before/after 12 0'; havellin.html:37276 (_invPicked ignores filters), 37298-37450 (_invBulkApply never clears), 29938

findings.title: The Contents Record the client signs can carry 'IN PROGRESS … may still change' and the sign-off together
findings.where: Contents Record; printContentsRecord havellin.html:35561 (_invProgressStamp 30613 plus contentsRecordSignoff 35655, which withholds only on undecided lines)
findings.evidence: b8.js: all 13 lines decided, none reviewed. The page prints 'IN PROGRESS — 0 of 13 items reviewed This is a working copy issued during the engagement. Values and dispositions on unreviewed lines may still change.' and, at its foot, 'Sign-off Reviewed and accepted as the record of what stayed and what left the property … Signature: ____ Joan Whitfield, Client'. Checks: has IN PROGRESS true, has Sign-off true, withheld false. Saved as LIV/b8-contents-unreviewed.html.
findings.tc_impact: The concierge hands over, for signature, a page that says it is a working copy. The stamp also speaks of 'Values' on the one paper that 'does not state what anything is worth'. A family member or their advisor can fairly read the signature as accepting a draft.
findings.proposal: contentsRecordSignoff withholds the sign-off while any line is unreviewed, as it already does while one is undecided, and says so: 'The sign-off is withheld: 13 items are not yet reviewed by your concierge.' The living stamp drops the word 'Values'. Anthony picks whether review or decision is the gate.
findings.vnote: Observed on a 12-line living house where every line was decided through real controls (Select all plus Set disposition Keep, and row selects) and none was reviewed. The Contents Record prints 'IN PROGRESS — 0 of 12 items reviewed … Values and dispositions on unreviewed lines may still change.' and also the Sign-off ('Reviewed and accepted as the record …'). The main proposal, withholding the sign-off until every line is reviewed, gates on review and goes against the Domain rule 'Review gates nothing; documents in progress are stamped IN PROGRESS and never withheld' (Inventory and estate documentation). The auditor did not say so. One part needs no rule change: the stamp says 'Values' on a paper that 'does not state what anything is worth'. _invProgressStamp already takes opts.noValues for exactly this, and printContentsRecord does not pass it. The stamp could also be reworded so a signature is not read as accepting a draft. Anthony to decide whether the sign-off should wait on review.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v3.js → v3.out: 'CR stamp IN PROGRESS — 0 of 12 items reviewed … Values and dispositions …', 'CR signoff OFFERED'; v3-contents.html; havellin.html:30613-30630, 35655-35667

findings.title: Home Transition and Home Editing sell through auction houses but have no proceeds statements
findings.where: Closing the job bar; jobTakesProceedsStatements havellin.html:34848 (Home Cleanout or estate only); _renderProceedsCard 34905; the ledger card 34674 still reports 'no proceeds recorded'
findings.evidence: b1.js, Home Transition with Kodner confirmed and a Sell line. The Closing body shows the Disposition Ledger with '1 line sold, consigned or at auction with no proceeds recorded.' and no Proceeds statements card. b5.js, Home Editing: Sell is offered ('—|Auction|Consign|…|Sell') and Closing lists 'Contents Record, donations' with no proceeds card. b5.js, Home Cleanout: '+ Record a statement' is there, and typing 'Kodner Galleries' ticked 6 of 6 lots.
findings.tc_impact: A downsizing client sending 30 lots to Kodner means opening 30 records and typing 60 Gross and Fees boxes from the statement: the four taps a lot that P25/Q39 removed for estates and cleanouts. Nothing checks the statement's totals, and the client's Contents Record 'Net received' stays blank until someone types every figure.
findings.proposal: jobTakesProceedsStatements answers true on any job with a line on INV_SALE_DISPOSITIONS (the living half of ledgerApplies). The card, proceedsLine and the reconciliation then reach Home Transition and Home Editing. The test that holds it equal to planTaskCtx's isDisposal moves with it.
findings.vnote: On a Home Transition with two Sell lines and one Consign line, the Closing bar shows the Disposition Ledger with '3 lines sold, consigned or at auction with no proceeds recorded.' and no Proceeds statements card. jobTakesProceedsStatements (34848) answers true only for home_cleanout or an estate, while the desk offers Sell, Consign and Auction on Home Transition. The proposal changes a rule that a test holds equal to planTaskCtx's isDisposal, but nothing on the Decided list covers it. Today the per-line Gross and Fees boxes in the record are the only way to enter proceeds, so 'typed by hand' is accurate.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v3.js → v3.out: 'CLOSING bar body … Disposition Ledger … 3 lines sold, consigned or at auction with no proceeds recorded.', 'Proceeds card present? false'; havellin.html:34848-34850, 34905-34906

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 (P4: CLAUDE.md, Firearms go only to a licensed dealer; tests/p4-firearms-dealer.test.js, browser step 119)
findings.title: A living client's own firearm on Keep or Move is 'held' for good, and the way out the desk offers does not exist
findings.where: Row strip '⚠ held' (_renderInvRow havellin.html:39634), the 'Firearms held' Needs-you chip (INV_WORK_FLAGS 37117), invReleaseBlocked 29983, the record's Firearm block; invWrittenReleaseNeeded 31243 leaves Keep and Move lines off the request; the bulk bar offers Record approval only for invWrittenReleasePicked
findings.evidence: b12.js, Hale l07 shotgun set to Move, then Keep. Row: '⚠ held'. Chip: 'Firearms held 1'. State: {blocked:true, written:false, transport:'authority'}. Record: 'Not cleared to carry: No written authority on file — select the line on Job Admin & Inv and press Record approval once the signed authority is back.' But no request ever carries a Keep or Move line, and b11.js shows Record approval offered on the bulk bar only for the Distribute shotgun. firearms-protocol.html covers 'a decedent's firearms' only.
findings.tc_impact: A client keeping their own shotgun leaves a warning and a chip that never clear, and an instruction that cannot be followed. 'Firearms held' stops meaning anything on living jobs.
findings.proposal: On living work a firearm on Keep or Move is not held. Its row reads, in grey, 'stays with the client — the client moves it, never the crew or the movers'. invReleaseBlocked and the chip skip it, and Agent One's Firearm note stays as it is. Ask Anthony for the one protocol sentence about a living client moving their own encased firearm.
findings.decided_conflict: Firearms: 'nothing moves without written authority' (Domain rules). A Keep line does not move, and on Move the client carries it, not Havellin.
findings.vnote: Partly confirmed, and partly overstated. Hale's shotgun l07 on Move, then on Keep: the row reads '⚠ held', the chip 'Firearms held 1', blocked:true and written:false. With it picked alone, the bulk bar offers no Record approval. printApprovalRequest refuses with 'Nothing is waiting on written approval'. Yet the record still says to 'press Record approval'. That is the real inconsistency, because Keep and Move are not in INV_RELEASE_DISPOSITIONS. 'Held for good' is wrong, though: the living record shows Authorized By and Approval Date boxes, and typing 'Robert Hale' and a date cleared it (blocked:false). On the proposal: for Keep nothing moves. For Move, 'the client moves it' sits against the firearms rule ('nothing moves without written authority; … nobody else carries one out, family included'), which the auditor named. firearms-protocol.html covers only a decedent's firearms (line 302).
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v1.js → v1.out: 'Move l07 {…blocked:true,written:false}', 'Move chip ["Firearms held 1"]', 'bulk bar with l07 (Keep) picked [… no Record approval]', 'request on Keep WHY Nothing is waiting…', 'authBy/approvalDate controls [authBy text, approvalDate date]', 'l07 after typing authority {…blocked:false…}'; havellin.html:29982, 30080, 31243-31246

findings.title: On living jobs, 'Unsure' flags sit on values for Keep, Move and Junk lines that no paper prints
findings.where: Needs-you chip 'Unsure' (INV_WORK_FLAGS havellin.html:37096); invLineUnsure 37245 (only estates are exempt, through agentValueInternal 38483); agentValueAuto 38873; invLineReviewed 37222 waits on agentValueUnreviewed
findings.evidence: b7.js, Agent Two answering low on household lots and furniture: 'UNSURE by disposition on a living job {Move:16, Donate:4, Keep:4, Junk:4}', chip 'Unsure 28', and 'Contents Record prints a value? false'. b1.js: Agent Two valued 120 of 120 living lines.
findings.tc_impact: The playbook says to work the Unsure lines first. On living work 24 of 28 are figures for things the client keeps or throws away, which no living paper shows. Every line's one tick also has to cover such a figure. These are flags cleared for nothing.
findings.proposal: On living work, a figure on a Keep, Move or Junk line is treated the way agentValueInternal treats an estate where counsel values: no 'unsure', and it does not hold up invLineReviewed. It stays on the desk for routing and the summary. Alternatively, Agent Two values only lines leaving to be sold, donated or given to a person. Anthony to choose.
findings.vnote: The code is as described. invLineUnsure (37245) exempts only agentValueInternal, which covers estates whose tier states no values. So on living work a low-confidence Agent Two figure on a Keep, Move or Junk line reads unsure. No living paper prints those figures: the Contents Record and the living ledger print no fmv, and the workbook states values only where fid holds (saveInventory.gs:253). The counts are the stub's, not the model's: my stub answered low on every ordinary lot and gave Unsure 36 = {Move 12, Donate 6, Keep 6, Sell 6, Junk 3}, so the auditor's 24 of 28 is also fixture-driven. Half the proposal goes against a Domain rule: a figure that 'does not hold up invLineReviewed' contradicts 'Every figure is unreviewed until looked at … the line's one tick covers its value'. Even the agentValueInternal precedent keeps agentValueUnreviewed in invLineReviewed. The alternative, 'Agent Two values only leaving lines', is against agentValueAuto ('every named line with a photograph', Anthony: 'Yes, run it by itself'). Dropping only the unsure hint on living Keep, Move and Junk lines would be compatible. LIV-19, meanwhile, wants these same Move figures as the mover's declared value.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v2.js → v2.out: STATE unsure {Move:12,Donate:6,Keep:6,Sell:6,Junk:3}, CHIPS 'Unsure 36' (stubbed low); havellin.html:37245-37253, 38483-38506, 37222-37227

findings.title: A name typed and decided at the desk is not reviewed, and correcting a name after ticking unticks the line
findings.where: Row's Reviewed box; invLineReviewed havellin.html:37222 (agentValueUnreviewed checked first); agentValueAfterRename 38921; _avWrite clears valReviewed
findings.evidence: b3.js, s5: typed 'Ethan Allen mahogany drop-leaf side table', then chose Keep: {by:'desk', disp:'Keep', rev:false, unrev:true}. Agent Two re-researched it (1 request, mode comps, nameChecked true) and it stayed rev:false. b11.js, l12: ticked Reviewed {rev:true}, renamed it 'Toro Recycler 22-inch self-propelled lawn mower', 1 agentValue request followed, then {rev:false, tick:true, valRev:false}. The box the concierge ticked unticked itself seconds later.
findings.tc_impact: CLAUDE.md says a line named on the desk with a disposition chosen is reviewed. That never holds on a job Agent Two has valued, which is every photographed line. Correcting a name costs a wait plus a second tick, and a box unticking itself reads as lost work.
findings.proposal: A person's rename stamps the review: the person looked. The re-value that follows keeps it reviewed, and the row says 'value updated for your name: $X' instead of reopening the line. At the least, the row shows 're-valuing…' and why the tick came off. Functions: _invEdit (objectName), _avWrite, invLineReviewed.
findings.vnote: The behaviour reproduces. l12: ticking gave rev:true. A rename sent one agentValue request {mode:comps, nameChecked:true}, and after the redraw the line read rev:false with the box unchecked and nothing on the row saying why. l14: a name typed on a blank line and Keep chosen never reads reviewed, because the typed name fires agentValueAfterRename at once and the new figure is unreviewed. CLAUDE.md does not say a desk-named, decided line is simply reviewed: it adds 'since 2026-10-25b no line is reviewed while it carries an agent figure nobody has looked at'. So the claimed inconsistency with the rulebook is not there. The main proposal, a rename stamping the review so the re-value lands reviewed, goes against the Domain rule 'Every figure is unreviewed until looked at' and Agent Two's rule 'a figure accepted for the old name is accepted no longer'. The fallback would be compatible: the row says 're-valuing for your new name' and why the tick came off.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v1.js → v1.out ('l12 after tick … rev:true', 'rename sent [{id:l12,mode:comps,nameChecked:true}]', 'l14 after value … rev:false'); LIV-verify/v4.js → v4.out ('l12 after rename + redraw {rev:false, reviewed:true, valRev:false, box:false}'); havellin.html:37222-37227, 38921-38932

findings.title: Photographs Agent One found nothing in stay as lines in Unnamed shots and block the client's sign-off
findings.where: Needs-you chip 'Unnamed shots' (INV_WORK_FLAGS havellin.html:37091, test !r.objectName); agentNameableRefs skips agentConf 'none'; dispositionRecord 35519 (counted unnamed and undecided); contentsRecordSignoff
findings.evidence: b1.js, 120 shots: the chip read 'Unnamed shots 10' while the work bar read '10 with nothing in frame' and no Name button was left. Rows read 'nothing to list'. The Contents Record read '122 items with no destination … 10 photographed items not yet named' and withheld the sign-off. b6.js: 33 such lines on a 400-shot house. The way out is 4 presses (chip, Select all, Remove lines, OK), and in b2.js that path ran into LIV-02.
findings.tc_impact: Every evening these lines sit in three piles (Unnamed, Not reviewed, Not yet decided) and show as gaps on the family's record until someone deletes them one batch at a time.
findings.proposal: One press on the naming summary: '10 photographs had nothing to list: Remove these 10 lines (the photographs stay)'. Give them their own chip, 'Nothing to list N', out of Unnamed shots, so Unnamed shots reaches 0 once naming is done.
findings.vnote: On a 36-shot house, 3 photographs came back agentConf 'none'. The chip read 'Unnamed shots 3' (the test is !r.objectName, havellin.html:37091), and the Contents Record listed '3 photographed items not yet named'. With no disposition they also count as undecided, and the sign-off was withheld. The only way out today is chip, Select all, Remove lines, OK, and that path is the one that runs into LIV-02. The proposal is allowed.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v2.js → v2.out: STATE none:3, CHIPS 'Unnamed shots 3', 'CR gaps … 3 photographed items not yet named', 'CR signoff withheld'; havellin.html:37091, 35548-35552

findings.title: The one paper a living client signs has no iPad signing and no send
findings.where: Contents Record card, Closing the job bar; _renderContentsCard havellin.html:35195 (offers File to Drive and File signed copy only); the work bar's Contents Record button prints straight away
findings.evidence: b1.js, Closing body: 'Contents Record (the record the client signs at close-out) … File to Drive File signed copy … No signed copy on file — the client signs it at close-out.' There is no sign or send control. The pad, the PDF and the filing path all exist: b4.js signed a donation on the pad and filed the PDF (htmlToPdf, uploadFile).
findings.tc_impact: Getting the signature means printing in the house, signing, scanning or photographing, then File signed copy: four steps or more. The client gets a copy only if the concierge emails one by hand.
findings.proposal: Add '✍ Sign on the iPad' to the Contents Record card, withheld while contentsRecordSignoff would withhold. The signature goes in place of the line. The PDF is made by _signoutPdf and filed by fileSignedCopy (kind contents, glass:true). A Gmail draft of the signed copy then goes to clientRecipient, as _agrIpadEmailCopy does for the agreement. Anthony, P28: 'signing things on the ipad is genius'.
findings.vnote: _renderContentsCard offers only File to Drive and File signed copy (code read, and v3's Closing body text); printing happens from the work bar. Nothing on the card signs on the pad or sends the paper. Small correction: File signed copy takes a photograph straight from the iPad, so it is print, sign, photograph, file, not a scan. Building on P28's pad, _signoutPdf and fileSignedCopy is allowed and nothing on the Decided list covers it. It is a new feature under the freeze, and it happens once per job, hence low.

findings.title: The donation papers do not give a donor's CPA what a deduction needs
findings.where: Donation Record (Donations card): printDonationRecord havellin.html:34755. Donation Release signed on the iPad: signoutSheetHtml's donation acknowledgement (~31735); openSignoutDialog prefills the signer with the charity's name (~31803)
findings.evidence: b4.js, Hale: the donation sheet signed on the pad reads 'I received the items listed above as a charitable donation from Robert Hale … This list records the delivery only; any valuation is the donor’s. Signed by: Goodwill Palm Beach , signed on the iPad · Oct 26, 2026' (LIV/b4-donation-sheet.html). Afterwards l02 read {gone:false, rcpt:true} and the Donation Record still printed 'Date donated —'. b9.js: the Donation Record printed Agent Two's unreviewed $350 as 'Havellin’s estimates' (l02 {valuedBy:'agent', valRev:false}). KNOWN: the leaving day prints '—'. The new impact is that the app now witnesses that day on the signed sheet and still prints nothing.
findings.tc_impact: A Palm Beach donor's CPA needs, for Form 8283: the date of the gift, a description, the condition, the value and the method behind it, and a qualified appraisal once similar items pass $5,000. The charity's acknowledgement needs the 'no goods or services' statement for gifts of $250 or more. The record has no date, no method and no $5,000 warning. The iPad sheet lacks the statement, and it names the charity rather than the person who signed.
findings.proposal: Donation Record: print the date donated from the filed sign-out's signedOn; add a method column ('Havellin estimate, second-hand market' or 'appraisal by …'); add an amber line where a category passes $5,000 ('a qualified appraisal is needed for the deduction'); show the condition grade. Donation Release: add 'No goods or services were provided in exchange for this donation', and ask for the signer's own name and title in a blank box. Send the wording to the counsel and CPA bundle.
findings.vnote: The core is confirmed, but the finding needs corrections. On the Donation Record (v3, lamps and TV to Goodwill), Date donated reads '—' from dispDate only, which is KNOWN. There is no $5,000 qualified-appraisal line, and the unreviewed agent figures $80 and $150 print. The charity's sign-out acknowledgement (31718) has no 'no goods or services' sentence, and its signer box is prefilled with the charity's name (openSignoutDialog: signer.value = g.taker). Three parts of the finding are wrong. Condition IS printed ('Good'; invConditionText), so 'show the condition grade' is moot. A method sentence exists: 'Values are Havellin's estimates of what each item would sell for … They are not appraisals', plus the deduction is deferred to the tax adviser. The receipt line prints the receipt's filed date ('filed <date>'), so 'no date even after the app witnessed it' holds only for the per-line column. The IRS points (§170(f)(8) acknowledgement for gifts of $250 or more; Form 8283 Section B above $5,000) are sound expert judgement I cannot test here. They matter most if the iPad sheet stands in for the charity's own receipt.
findings.vrepro: LIV-verify/v3.js → v3.out: 'DONATION … Condition Date donated Estimated value … Good — $80 … Values are Havellin’s estimates …', 'has "no goods or services"? false | $5,000 warning? false'; havellin.html:31718, printDonationRecord, openSignoutDialog (signer.value = g.taker)
